title: Kafka-based log shaper with tenant-aware fanout and correlation-id enrichment
creator: Priya Raman
description: Build a resilient Kafka-based ingestion layer that normalizes and validates incoming structured logs, enriches records with tracing correlation IDs when missing, performs tenant-aware fanout, and routes to Loki with label extraction. The pipeline must provide strong backpressure characteristics, observable metrics, and PII redaction capabilities. This ticket implements the core shaping and streaming transformations, plus the initial Grafana dashboards and alerts for operational health.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress accepts protobuf/JSON logs from producers and writes normalized JSON to a Kafka topic
Records missing correlation_id are enriched using tracing hooks (traceparent/header) or a generated UUID and annotated in metadata
Schema validator rejects invalid records to a dead-letter Kafka topic with reason codes
Tenant-aware fanout writes per-tenant topics or partitions; single-tenant messages are isolated from other tenants
Sink connector converts normalized records into Loki push API batches with label extraction and multiline log support
Redaction stage removes PII based on a configurable ruleset before sinks; redaction metrics emitted
Prometheus metrics exposed: ingress_rate, parse_failures, enrichment_failures, kafka_lag, fanout_latency, redaction_count
End-to-end latency for 95th percentile under normal load < 350ms and under burst < 1s with backpressure engaged
Dashboards (Grafana) for latency, parse failure trends, tenant lag heatmap, and correlation-id coverage
Runbook created with triage steps, SLOs, and escalation contacts
tasks: Design JSON Schema and enums for canonical log record
Implement Kafka consumer shaping service (Go) with parallel schema validation
Add correlation-id enrichment module hooking into tracing headers
Implement PII redaction rules and unit tests
Create dead-letter topic format and error classification
Build Loki sink connector and batching strategy
Add per-tenant routing policy and config UI flags
Instrument Prometheus metrics and OpenTelemetry traces
Create Grafana dashboards and alert rules
Write migration script for existing raw-logs -> shaped-logs topic
Run controlled canary in eu-west-1 with 10% traffic for 48 hours
notes: We decided against using Fluentd for the shaping stage because we need deterministic schema validation and lower tail latency; a Go service gives better control over batching and backpressure.
Correlation-id enrichment: prefer extracting W3C traceparent header; fallback order: traceparent -> x-request-id -> generate uuidv4
Redaction must be configurable per-namespace; maintain allowlist and denylist patterns in a secured S3 JSON file downloaded by the shaping service
Fanout approach: use topic per-tenant for high-volume tenants, partitioned by ingestion shard for throughput; smaller tenants share a multiplexed topic with tenant label to conserve topics.
For Loki labels, avoid overly cardinal labels. Extract service, environment, tenant_id, request_type. Keep user_id and email redacted unless explicitly whitelisted.
Backpressure: rely on Kafka consumer group pause/resume and producer throttling. For extreme overload, route to short-term S3 staging and emit alert.
Compatibility: provide an ELK-compatible output mode that writes to an intermediate JSON indexer topic for teams still consuming via Logstash
Retention: shaped-logs topic default retention 14d; dead-letter topic retention 7d unless escalated by PM
